detailed_rationale: [DATA] FY26 (year ended Mar-2026): standalone PAT Rs.10,527cr, consolidated PAT ~Rs.10,306cr (sum of quarterly consol prints 3,089+2,814+2,576+1,831=10,310cr, internally consistent). Q4FY26 standalone PAT Rs.3,741cr (+14.7% YoY); Q4FY26 consol ~Rs.3,089cr. GNPA improved 3.27% (Mar-25) -> 2.26% (Dec-25) -> 1.98% (Mar-26); NNPA 0.82% -> 0.60% -> 0.56% over the same three points - a monotonic two-quarter improvement, not a single-quarter jump. CRAR 17.77% -> 17.09% -> 18.01% (Basel III), aided by Rs.2,500cr Tier-II + Rs.10,000cr infra bonds raised Dec-25. RoA 0.98% (Q4FY25) -> 0.96% (Q3FY26) -> 1.01% (Q4FY26). Dividend Rs.4.65/sh (46.5% payout), paid 15-Jul-26. [INFERENCE] Write-back/one-off check: sector-wide PSU-bank data (Business Standard/Daily Excelsior, FY26) shows aggregate PSB GNPA falling to 1.93% and NNPA to 0.39% with slippage ratio down to 0.7% and write-offs at multi-year LOWS (i.e. banks recovering/upgrading rather than book-cleaning via write-off) - BOI's trend tracks this sector pattern directionally, arguing the improvement is credit-cycle-driven rather than a single quarter's write-back spike. However I could NOT find a BOI-specific slippage/recovery/write-off bps breakdown (searched, not surfaced) - so the exact composition (cash recovery vs technical write-off vs upgradation) is a genuine data gap, tagged [INFERENCE] not [DATA]. NIM and CASA ratio for BOI Q4FY26 were NOT found in sources checked (screener.in explicitly flags this as undisclosed/limited in its own summary) - data gap, not fabricated. Governance: MD&CEO Rajneesh Karnatak's tenure was extended 3 years from 29-Apr-2026 (ACC/Cabinet approved alongside BoB's CEO) - this binary is RESOLVED, no overhang. Govt stake 73.38% - well within the 75% ceiling and NOT among the banks (e.g. IOB at 92.44%) facing forced SEBI 25%-public-float dilution by Aug-2026, so no near-term forced-dilution overhang specific to BOI. Q1FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter): provisional business update already out - global business +16.58% YoY to Rs.17.56 lakh cr, deposits +14.92% YoY to Rs.9.58 lakh cr, advances +18.64% YoY to Rs.7.97 lakh cr - but full P&L/GNPA results were STILL PENDING as of 20-Jul-2026 (a bank-results compilation dated 18/20-Jul-2026 listed BOI's profit column blank while peers Union Bank/PNB/Indian Bank/BoM/IOB/CBoI had already reported). Valuation: CMP ~Rs.144-147, P/E ~6.3-6.5x, P/B ~0.74x, book value ~Rs.198-210/sh, ROE ~12.4% (3yr avg 11.7%), ROCE ~5.93% (screener.in flags ROCE/interest-coverage as weak vs banking peers).
recommendation_rationale: No quant score exists yet for BANKINDIA in the STOCK_SCORECARD run, so per V1 asymmetric-override rules the default is Hold absent an escalation-worthy red flag. Nothing found here rises to that bar: asset quality is improving on a multi-quarter trend (not a one-off), capital is adequate and freshly topped up, the CEO-tenure binary is resolved, and the government-stake dilution overhang that hits some peers (IOB) does not apply to BOI. The main caveats - unresolved NIM/CASA disclosure gaps, weak ROCE, and P/B math suggesting the stock is roughly fair-to-slightly-rich rather than deeply undervalued despite a headline-cheap P/E - are watch items, not sell triggers. Hold, no escalation.
summary: [DATA] Bank of India: FY26 standalone PAT Rs.10,527cr; GNPA down to 1.98% / NNPA 0.56% (Mar-26) from 3.27%/0.82% a year ago, improving each of the last two quarters; CRAR 18.01%; RoA 1.01%. CEO tenure extended to 2029 (overhang resolved); govt stake 73.38%, not facing forced SEBI-float dilution unlike some PSU peers. Trades at P/E ~6.3x, P/B ~0.74x. Q1FY27 (Jun-26) full results PENDING as of 20-Jul-2026; provisional business update shows advances +18.64% YoY, deposits +14.92% YoY. [INFERENCE] Asset-quality improvement tracks a sector-wide PSU-bank pattern of falling slippages/write-offs (genuine cycle, not obviously one-off) but BOI-specific slippage/recovery composition and NIM/CASA were not disclosed in sources checked - data gaps, not red flags.
positive_para: [DATA] Two consecutive quarters of GNPA/NNPA improvement (3.27%/0.82% Mar-25 -> 2.26%/0.60% Dec-25 -> 1.98%/0.56% Mar-26) rather than a single-quarter jump, which is harder to dismiss as pure optics. CRAR at 18.01% post a Rs.12,500cr capital raise (Tier-II + infra bonds) gives comfortable growth headroom. RoA crossed 1% in Q4FY26 (0.98% a year earlier), and FY26 standalone PAT of Rs.10,527cr marks a step-change in profitability. Q1FY27 provisional numbers show strong balance-sheet momentum: advances +18.64% YoY, deposits +14.92% YoY, global business +16.58% YoY. Governance overhang removed - MD&CEO Rajneesh Karnatak's term was extended 3 years (to 2029) by the ACC, and BOI's 73.38% government stake keeps it clear of the forced-dilution timeline squeezing higher-govt-stake peers like IOB (92.44%). Valuation is undemanding on a headline basis at P/E ~6.3-6.5x.
negative_para: [DATA/INFERENCE] ROE of ~12.4% (3yr avg 11.7%) and ROCE of ~5.93% remain weak versus private-bank peers and even versus some PSU peers, and a reverse P/B check (Gordon-growth: P/B = (ROE-g)/(COE-g)) using ROE~12.4%, an estimated PSU-bank cost of equity ~14% and terminal growth ~9% implies a 'fair' P/B near 0.65-0.70x - close to the actual 0.74x - meaning the stock looks roughly fairly valued on normalized ROE, not a screaming bargain despite the low P/E; the classic PSU-bank value-trap risk (cheap P/E, structurally sub-cost-of-equity ROE) is not resolved. [DATA] NIM and CASA ratio for BOI - the two clearest read-throughs on core franchise quality and margin durability - were NOT found/disclosed in the sources checked for this cycle, a real transparency gap. [INFERENCE] The GNPA/NNPA improvement, while multi-quarter and sector-consistent, still lacks a BOI-specific slippage/recovery/write-off breakdown, so the degree to which FY26's profit surge is credit-cost-normalization (a fading tailwind once GNPA is already near cycle lows) versus durable core-NII growth cannot be fully separated from data in hand. Q1FY27 full P&L (including whether the asset-quality trend continues) is still pending disclosure as of 20-Jul-2026, a near-term event risk/unknown.
reverse_dcf_judgment: [INFERENCE] At P/B ~0.74x with ROE ~12.4% and an assumed PSU-bank cost of equity ~13-14%, the Gordon-growth-implied fair P/B (ROE-g)/(COE-g) with g~8-9% comes out near 0.65-0.72x - i.e. the market price is roughly in line with, perhaps a touch above, what current normalized ROE justifies. This is NOT a deep-value / margin-of-safety setup on P/B despite the low headline P/E (~6.3-6.5x, itself partly a base-effect artifact of FY26's asset-quality-driven profit jump). Re-rating from here needs either a genuine, sustained ROE improvement above ~14-15% (durable NIM/fee income gains, not just falling credit cost) or continued loan-book compounding at the ~18% pace seen in the Q1FY27 business update feeding through to core PPOP - neither confirmed yet pending Q1FY27 full disclosure.
